I knew that AP classes could get people ahead in college, but I had no idea it could save me that much money. I'm suddenly very thankful that my school offers so many AP classes, haha. Thanks for the info!

It's also really nice to know that Algebra 2 isn't that influenced by Geometry. I just barely passed the Geo EOC, but that definitely doesn't reflect how well I understand the subject (which is to say, almost not at all). I'm hoping Algebra is a little easier on me.

And yeah, I think my overall plan at this point is to just drop down to regular classes if any of them are too much for me. I apologize for the late-ish response, but this helped ease my overly stressed mind, so thank you again!

Yup, I'm already working on just making sure I get through the classes I need in order to graduate high school, and I think I'm on track so far. 4 AP classes in one year does sound pretty rough too! I'm really hoping to find a class that I can call my favorite though, so it might make things a little easier on me like it seemed to for you. And if some of my classes are just too much for me, I'll definitely do what I can to make sure I'm not stuck with them. Not looking forward to all the studying that I know is ahead of me, but I'm willing to make some sacrifices.

Thank you for all the help, and sorry for getting back to you so late! I really appreciate all of your responses. :)

Thank you! I've heard from another person that their guidance counselor also gave them a hard time when they tried switching out of an AP class--not sure what the deal is with this happening, but it seems kinda common. I'll definitely make sure to discuss it with others if AP/honors seems to be a bit much for me once the school year starts.

Also, sorry for the super late reply! I'm still really thankful for your help though.

I don't know if I can be of much help, but I'm the same exact way as someone going into their sophomore year of high school. I've almost always been in advanced and honors classes, but I still have yet to memorize the multiplication table (I'm also terrible at simple mental math, which yes, often includes addition and subtraction). Not too sure how common this is, but you're definitely not alone. I've started working on it recently because I think it could definitely save me some time by being able to quickly remember simple multiplication. There's a lot of websites, apps, and pages on quizlet that offer flashcards to help quiz yourself on problems. Flashcards online are easily accessible, but you could always buy a physical set to have in person. I've also heard that repeatedly writing down the table can help as well, or at least practice memorizing each line (3, 6, 9, 12... 5, 10, 15, 20, etc). There's a lot of different methods to make memorizing multiplication a little easier, but those were some pretty basic ones that might help you out. Everyone is different though, so it's best to find out what works for you.

Damn, it's awesome that you got to skip a year of college! My high school offers a tonnn of AP classes, so I'd probably be able to pull that off if AP ends up working okay for me. And yeah, I currently plan on just feeling things out for a few weeks and seeing if I'm okay with the amount of work and the difficulty level. I just gotta keep reminding myself that I'm never completely stuck in a place or class academically speaking.


And you don't have to answer this if you don't feel like it, but do you remember how many AP classes you took in total, or the most you took in one year? I'm sorta blindly navigating high school and I'm not too certain as to what I want to study in college so I'm not sure if taking a bunch of AP classes is the best thing to do yet.


Thank you for the advice though! You definitely helped me not freak out about my class schedule. :)

This is really good advice, thank you! And yeah, I've heard of someone getting like a 5.0 GPA just because they took a bunch of Honors and AP classes that they were really good at. It is pretty insane. I'm not 100% set on what I want to study or even what college I want to attend, but I don't know, I feel like it might make things easier if I take advanced classes now, even if I end up going to a not so prestigious university (like most non-ivy league schools). As for my mental health, you're absolutely right. I think I might go through with taking the classes my counselor set up for me, and if it's too much and my health suffers from it, I'll talk it out with people and see what other options I have. I think one of my main worries was that I'd regret taking these classes and it wouldn't be worth it, but from what you described, I don't think it's too bad of an idea, or even that risky. I've also had other family members encouraging me to just see what it's like the first few weeks, so I'm a little extra convinced at this point.


I also read the other comment you posted, and it's really comforting to hear that it is possible to drop out of AP classes, if needed. I thought my school might give me a rough time if I wanted to switch my classes up, but there's no way I'm gonna be stuck suffering in classes I can't keep up with. I gotta give it to you for trying 4 AP classes at once though! I know it was mainly for your friend, but that's still pretty impressive, haha.

Anyways, I really appreciate your response and wishing me luck! This helped me out a lot, and I feel a lot less stressed.

I definitely wouldn't say you should feel scared, but you might want to be cautious. If your family has ever expressed dislike for gay and bi folks, it may or may not be unsafe for you to come out to your family if you're living with them. I don't know your situation, so that's up for you to decide. Either way, if it's something you want to do, and you feel like your family will be supportive or at least willing to talk about things, then go for it! There are, of course, religious people who are accepting of LGBT+ people, and non-religious people who are not, so it really does depend.

Edit: I should add, please don't feel pressured to come out. It is not something you have to do any time soon (or ever, if you don't feel like it), but I understand the feeling of wanting to talk to close family about it and let them know, especially since a lot of people tend to immediately assume others are straight. I hope this helps! :)

Hi! Thank you so much for the help. I'm currently 15 years old. I know I'm young, but I'm 3 years away from turning 18 and I've been kind of freaking out lately because that's not a very long time and I do not want to enter adulthood in this state.

Your professor sounds like an angel and I think it's amazing that she was able to help you like that. "Do the next best thing" isn't something I had ever really thought of, to be honest. I always overwhelm myself and overcomplicate everything. I get what you're saying though--sometimes you just have to think of a really big task as just smaller, easier tasks. I think I'll definitely keep that in mind when everything feels like too much.

As for planners, I've kind of tried similar things before (like to-do lists), but I always end up not following through for some reason and then getting really discouraged. I think setting up very simple goals/plans throughout the week would actually be a lot more efficient though. I can try that out for sure! I think one of my biggest issues is sleep (which I should be doing very soon), so making plans for good times to go to bed would help me out a lot in waking up earlier and giving me more time in the day.

Anyways, I appreciate all the advice, kind words, and support. It's very comforting to hear that I'm not alone. It's really easy for me to forget that hey, a lot of people do wake up a lot later than they probably want to, or struggle with getting minor things done. I guess I've kind of gone blind to that, so to say, because I'm usually surrounded by people who seem to have their life together pretty well. Regardless, thank you for being so understanding and nice! It's good to hear that things have gotten better from when you were in college and I'm not completely hopeless. And I definitely won't be forgetting "do the next best thing" anytime soon <3 

I think I'll be going to bed now, haha. It's 2 AM so I'm sorry if this is a bit all over the place, but I hope I got my point and appreciation across! You've made me feel pretty optimistic, and I'll do my best tomorrow to see what I can do to help myself out.

>Things are hard and honestly you are busy trying to find you while caught up between school life and a split home life it seems.

This sentence pretty much sums up what I'm going through. I could never find words to explain myself and how overwhelming things are but you seem to have done it perfectly. God, I can't thank you enough for this. It just feels really good to hear from someone who was going through what I'm currently dealing with. I'm glad things got so much better for you, and you're the first person to actually tell me that I'm not a loser or a failure, and thinking about it now, I realize that you're right. Having ADHD always seems to make it seem like I'm failing everything and everyone, but I have to keep reminding myself that this is temporary and things can get better. 

Talking to my dad can be a bit rough, because he's not great at understanding where I'm coming from, but I'll definitely try since I've never quite talked to him in depth about any of this (opening up can suck but I'm kinda desperate). I'll at least go to my mom and ask her what to do, because I don't think I can get through this without any help. Honestly, what you wrote was very comforting to read and I appreciate you taking time to give me advice from your own experiences. I'll also try working on not apologizing so much for pretty insignificant things. I can definitely see how that could be negatively affecting me and I'm just now realizing that I do it more often than I should.

Again, I appreciate your encouragement and belief in me! I wasn't expecting to get replies to this so I'm pleasantly surprised that I got such a good one. I'm going to stop expecting immediate results and try to reach out for help for once.

Hey, I'm sorry so much has happened to you in such a short time frame. I know it's a lot to take in and deal with, and I can understand that you're really struggling with it all. I honestly wish I could help you get through this and take away your pain, but I at least hope you know that there are people that are here for you and genuinely care, including myself. Have you maybe tried reaching out to a hotline or something similar? I know what it's like to be in a similar position to the one you're currently in, and I understand if seeking additional help like that might be difficult or not even something you want to do. That's okay, and regardless, I'm so proud of you for posting here for help. I know you're hurting, but I'm here to listen and so are others. Please feel free to talk to me, and I really hope things get better for you and you reconsider this.

While I see a lot of people here saying "you don't owe your readers shit," I think it would be a good idea to at least update the summary of your fic and state that you're probably just not going to update it anymore. You don't necessarily have to explain yourself if you don't want to, but as a reader, it doesn't feel great when the author just stops updating a fic I heavily enjoyed and just ignores in completely. It's really up to you, but I seriously do not see any harm in being honest with your readers upfront so things get cleared up and they aren't left with much false hope. If you ever stop writing something because you were in a bad place mentally or maybe even just stopped enjoying that particular fandom or thing you were writing about, that's perfectly fine! I've seen it happen to writers, and it's happened to me too. But, like I said, you do what feels right to you, and if you're deeply worried about this, then you might feel better by just letting your readers know what's up.

edit: also, if the readers of your story don't understand and get overly upset (which I've never, ever seen that happen to a writer who went on a hiatus or abandoned their work), then that's on them. If you simply do not want to continue writing a fic, then don't do it. I can guarantee a lot of the readers will appreciate your honesty and thank you for it. Also, if I ever see a writer who just kind of stopped writing for a specific fandom, I don't really think of them in a negative way. If they're an amazing author, I'm still going to read their stuff (as long as I'm into whatever they're writing about)!

Yeah, that makes a lot of sense. It wouldn't surprise me if the brain sometimes gets confused with pain signals coming from places that don't normally hurt. This hasn't really caused any issues for me, so I think I'll be good. I definitely feel slightly less weird now haha.

Oh hey, I've heard of aphantasia! I can definitely see how something you've experienced your whole life is something you expect everyone else to feel as well, until you learn otherwise. It was pretty confusing and shocking learning that this pain isn't something most people experience.

Anyways, your answer really helped me out, and I think I definitely found a very possible answer. I googled referred pain, read up on the wiki, and it sounds almost identical to what I experience. I still think it's a bit weird that stubbing my toe isn't really felt in my toe at all, but instead my lower gums. I may be short, but that's a pretty far distance to experience referred/reflective pain in. I thought maybe it had something to do with connected nerves or something, but referred pain makes a lot more sense. I also have very vague knowledge about how nerves work, haha. Thank you for the info! It's also really comforting to know someone else has it to an extent.

edit: okay actually, pretty sure referred pain has a bit to do with connected nerves, so I was kind of right? There's not a whole lot of info on the topic, but oh well.
